items.title: Fixed #33882 -- async with transaction.atomic.

labels.name: coverage
labels.description: Generate a comment with a coverage diff

items.body:
#### Trac ticket number

ticket-33882

#### Branch description

See [this comment](https://code.djangoproject.com/ticket/33882#comment:29) on trac.

We are adding async support to `transaction.atomic` so that `async with transaction.atomic` can work.
I have been in communication with @carltongibson regarding this work.

This PR depends on https://github.com/django/asgiref/pull/596.

As described on the related asgiref PR, there were two designs I explored. The advantage of the design in this current PR where an executor is provided to the `ThreadSensitiveContext` is that it allows a future optimization where django (the `transaction.atomic` calling context) could maintain a pool of executors for re-use, allowing also reuse of threads and more importantly connections, if CONN_MAX_AGE allows.  In the alternative design not shown here, there is simply a new `force_new_thread` param to the `ThreadSensitiveContext` initializer and the executor construction logic is kept inside asgiref's `SyncToAsync.__call__` method.

I already have some code for the optimization described above, but that can be explored later in a separate PR depending on what we decide to do here.

items.title: Refs #28905 -- Declared optional dependencies in pyproject.toml
items.body:
#### Trac ticket number

ticket-28905

#### Branch description

Declares all of Django's optional Python dependencies in `pyproject.toml`, making
them installable as pip extras (e.g. `pip install "django[postgresql,gis]"`).
Replaces the `tests/requirements/` directory with PEP 735 dependency groups,
consolidating all dependency management into a single file. Adds a new
documentation page covering every optional extra with purpose, version
requirements, and install instructions.

**pip extras added** (`[project.optional-dependencies]`)

New extras: `admindocs`, `colorama`, `geoip`, `gis`, `images`, `jinja2`,
`mysql`, `oracle`, `postgresql`, `postgresql-pool`, `pylibmc`, `pymemcache`,
`pywatchman`, `redis`, `selenium`, `test-parallel`, `yaml`. The existing
`argon2` and `bcrypt` extras are unchanged.

**PEP 735 dependency groups added** (`[dependency-groups]`)

Six groups replace `tests/requirements/*.txt`: `test`, `postgres`, `mysql`,
`oracle`, and the composed `test-postgres`, `test-mysql`, `test-oracle`. All
GitHub Actions workflows updated to use `--group` (requires pip 25.1+).

**Notable decisions**

- `postgresql` vs `postgresql-pool`: the base extra installs only `psycopg`
  for basic connectivity; `postgresql-pool` additionally installs `psycopg-pool`
  for projects using Django's server-side connection pooling. The
  `ImproperlyConfigured` error message when pool support is missing now
  references `django[postgresql-pool]`.

- `psycopg` (no `[binary]`) for user-facing extras, `psycopg[binary]` for CI
  dependency groups: production Linux users link against system `libpq`; CI
  runners do not need it.

- `colorama` carries a `sys_platform == 'win32'` marker — it is only useful
  on Windows and the marker makes that constraint explicit.

- No `all` or `standard` bundle extra: Django has mutually exclusive database
  backends and platform-restricted extras, making a catch-all extra
  impractical. Granular extras let users compose exactly what they need.
  
#### Notes for mergers

The `tests/requirements/*.txt` files (`py3.txt`, `postgres.txt`, `mysql.txt`, `oracle.txt`) are
kept in this PR but marked as **deprecated**. The Jenkins CI infrastructure scripts
(outside this repository) still reference those files across multiple workflows
(postgres, mysql, oracle, gis, etc.). Those scripts will need to be updated to
use `pip install --group` before those files can be removed. Once Jenkins CI is
updated, a follow-up commit can drop them entirely.

items.title: Fixed #36027 -- Made error response rendering thread-sensitive.
items.body:
#### Trac ticket number
<!-- Replace XXXXX with the corresponding Trac ticket number. -->
<!-- Or delete the line and write "N/A - typo" for typo fixes. -->

ticket-36027

#### Branch description

Error response handling frequently makes use of the database, and so must use the request specific connection sensitive worker thread.

Previously response_for_exception was dispatched on the event loop's default executor. This potentially leads to pool exhaustion, and deadlock, when using database pooling options, or a large number of permanently held open database connections when not using pooling.

Connections held open were not subject to cleanup. If closed server side, the reported "connection is closed" would be seen until application restart.

Moving error response rendering to the request specific connection sensitive worker thread resolves both of these issues.

The `thread_sensitive=False` was set in
e17ee4468875077b90b70bb6a589ebad7493f757 to maintain the prior behaviour when asgiref switched the thread_sensitive default to `True`. There was no specific reason for the non-tread-sensitive behaviour beyond that. (With hindsight it was always incorrect for the reasons here.)

items.body:

#### Branch description
Issue: RedisCache async methods were using sync_to_async wrappers instead of redis-py's native async client, causing thread overhead and preventing proper full-page caching in async views.

items.body:
# Trac ticket number

N/A

# Branch description
Aims to address [this flakey ci failure](https://djangoci.com/job/pull-requests-pg-server-side-binding/database=postgres,label=focal-pr,python=python3.12/6005/testReport/backends.postgresql.tests/Tests/test_connect_pool/) for `postgresql.tests.Tests.test_connect_pool`

```
psycopg_pool.PoolTimeout: couldn't get a connection after 0.10 sec
```

When not set, the [default timeout value is 30 seconds](https://www.psycopg.org/psycopg3/docs/api/pool.html). 
During the development of the connection pool feature, testing locally 30 seconds was very slow and so I updated to 0.1 seconds to get quick feedback on failures. This value might be too quick for the ci on occasions and hoping 5 seconds is a good compromise.
